s: If this type comes, solve like this

s.q: If it asks the rank of a word in dictionary order (or the word at a given rank)
s.n: Go left to right; at each position count words that start with a smaller available letter. Divide by factorials of repeated letters left.

s.q: If letters of a word with repeats are arranged with together / not together conditions
s.n: Gap method for "no two X together": arrange others, choose gaps for X.

s.q: If it selects letters from a word with repeated letters (selection, not arrangement)
s.f: \text{case-split by pattern: all different / one pair / two pairs / \ldots}

s.q: If it counts numbers formed from digits with size or divisibility conditions
s.f: \text{fix the leading digit(s) by cases};\ 3:\ \text{digit sum};\ 11:\ \text{alternating sum};\ 4:\ \text{last two digits}
s.n: Split by the first digit relative to the bound (e.g. $>4321$). For divisibility by 11 with fixed digits, choose which digits go to odd/even places so the two sums differ by a multiple of 11.

s.q: If it counts digit-sum or digit-product conditions (sum of digits $=14$, product $=36$)
s.f: x_1+\cdots+x_k=S,\ 0\le x_i\le9:\ \text{stars and bars minus overflow cases}
s.n: For products, factor into digits ($36=4\cdot9=6\cdot6=2\cdot2\cdot9=\ldots$) and count arrangements of each multiset.

s.q: If it selects a committee/team with at-least conditions
If it distributes identical objects (integer solutions)
s.f: x_1+\cdots+x_r=n,\ x_i\ge0:\ {}^{n+r-1}C_{r-1};\ \ \text{lower bounds: subtract first};\ \ \text{upper bounds: inclusion–exclusion}
s.n: Distinct values ($x,y,z$ distinct): count all, subtract cases with equal values.

s.q: If it distributes distinct objects into boxes/groups (possibly identical boxes)
s.f: \text{distinct into identical non-empty boxes: Stirling } S(n,k);\ \ \text{into distinct boxes: } k^n \text{ (onto via inclusion–exclusion)}

s.q: If geometry counting: triangles/lines from points on sides or a polygon
s.f: {}^nC_3-\sum{}^{n_i}C_3\ \ (\text{remove collinear triples});\ \ \text{polygon triangles with no common side}: \frac{n(n-4)(n-5)}6

s.q: If it is a number-theory count (HCF, divisors of special form, $3^n\mid50!$)
If it involves subsets with sum/product conditions or no two consecutive
s.f: \text{no two consecutive from } n:\ \text{Fibonacci } F_{n+2};\ \text{use residues mod } k \text{ for sums}

s.q: If it is circular seating or derangements
s.f: (n-1)!;\ \ \text{girls not together at round table: } (b-1)!\cdot{}^bP_g;\ \ D_n=n!\sum\frac{(-1)^k}{k!}

s.q: If it is a factorial/${}^nP_r$ identity or a sum like $\sum k\cdot{}^kP_k$
